name: woodgrain
notes: Wood grain running round a knot, smoke curl: a scale-free wedge rather than a ring, so the grain has fine and coarse lines together instead of one thread width, then warped so it flows. Rides the SHALLOW RIGID train (dual scatter 0.2, spacing 0.28, n=3) because the warp makes its curves PHASE structure, and a deep train averages independent windows and blends curves away. Measured both ways on this family: three-quarters more delivered contrast on the rigid train at equal ripple (docs/spectral-atlas.md §4). tonal.gain 1.7 is the shallower train's compensation. From the spectral sweep in docs/spectral-atlas.md; levels 30/55/80 are damage DEPTH, not coverage - moderate damage renders as moderate contrast over intact paint. Verified by tools/spectrum-audit.mjs. Dual spacing tightened to 0.14 (from the family default 0.28): the rigid train leaves a deterministic count staircase at 1/spacing whose amplitude goes as 1/n, and this spectrum carries enough coarse power to sit right on it - the line measured 7.3% of tone before and 2.5% after, for about a fifth of the delivered contrast. tonal.gain follows n down. REVISED on review: crest axis turned 90 degrees (sectorAxisDeg 90) so the grain runs along the mark, which is both what wood does and the better measurement (8.4% -> 9.5%).
